title: Threshold-led rollouts flow and wireframes
body:
Goal and context:

This note captures an alternate approach to the rollouts console focused on threshold-driven step-ups/step-downs and minimal operator friction during canary and A/B experiments. The intention is to produce a small set of wireframe annotations + operator microcopy + backlog items that the design and eng teams can iterate on. This doc is intentionally prescriptive about heuristics so engineering can start prototyping with concrete rules.

Design principles (quick):
- Safer-by-default: any automatic progression requires an explicit SLO/CQ threshold and a kill-switch visible in the same surface.
- Lightweight operator flow: surface the minimum knobs for most customers (traffic %, metric thresholds, rollback hysteresis).
- Explainability: on-hover explanations and a short timeline view of what triggered each traffic change.
- Localizable microcopy and small copy footprint for dense operator screens.

High-level flow summary:
1) Create rollout: choose target routes and variants (model v1, v2, fallback pool).
2) Attach guardrails: select up-step and down-step thresholds, primary metric, evaluation window.
3) Simulate: instant backtest on recent traffic slice (10k requests) with expected metric curve overlay.
4) Start canary: console shows a compact timeline and real-time metric band.
5) Auto-step logic runs every evaluation window; operators can pause/unpause and see reasoning for decisions.

Wireframe annotations (left-to-right top panel layout):
- Top bar: rollout name, state chip (Draft / Running / Paused / Complete), small Abort button (red).
- Left column (config): target routes dropdown, variant selector (visual chips with small perf badge), traffic schedule mode (Manual | Threshold-led).
- Middle column (safety panel): primary metric selector, success threshold (e.g., p95 latency < 230ms), tolerance window (e.g., 3 consecutive windows), comparison baseline (baseline = production variant or historical median).
- Right column (live view): timeline sparkline with shaded confidence band, recent decisions list (timestamped); each decision item includes reason (metric delta), action (step +5% or rollback), and quick action buttons (Pause, Revert Last Step).

Microcopy examples (compact):
- Metric selector help text: "Pick the single metric that should drive progression (latency, error rate, regression score). Auto-step will compare current window to baseline."
- Up-step threshold label: "Advance when primary metric is within X% of baseline for Y windows."
- Down-step description: "If primary metric regresses beyond this threshold for Y windows, reduce traffic by Z% and pause auto-playback."
- Abort button tooltip: "Abort immediately: routes will be restored to baseline and rollout archived. Use only when user-facing impact is unacceptable."

Threshold-led heuristics (concrete proposal, copy/paste for eng):
- evaluation_window: 60s (configurable)
- sample_minimum: 200 requests per window
- primary_metric: configured by operator (string: e.g., "p95_latency_ms")
- baseline_comparison: delta pct = (candidate_metric - baseline_metric) / baseline_metric * 100
- advance_condition: delta_pct <= advance_threshold_pct for consecutive_windows_to_advance
- rollback_condition: delta_pct >= rollback_threshold_pct for consecutive_windows_to_rollback
- advance_step_size: +5% traffic (configurable), max_concurrency cap respected by serving side
- rollback_step_size: -50% or hard revert to baseline (operator choice)
- cooldown_after_rollback: 10m where auto-advance disabled

Example parameter set (recommended defaults):
- advance_threshold_pct: 3
- rollback_threshold_pct: 7
- consecutive_windows_to_advance: 2
- consecutive_windows_to_rollback: 1
- advance_step_size: 5
- rollback_behavior: "partial" (reduce 50%)

Edge cases and operator expectations:
- Low volume routes: if sample_minimum not met, auto-advance should remain disabled and UI should show "insufficient traffic" badge. Provide a manual step override with a confirmation modal that surfaces risk.
- Metric spikes: use median filter + outlier suppression (ignore values > 5 sigma) in displayed timeline and in decision calc. Decision engine uses trimmed mean across the observation window.
- Mixed signals across metrics: UI should allow a primary metric plus a secondary 'tiebreaker' metric. When primary passes but secondary fails, highlight conflict and pause progression until operator approves.
- Model-specific regressions: if quality regressions are detected (e.g., evaluation set prompt failures), auto-step must stop immediately and mark rollout Paused with 'quality-failure' tag.

Operator quick actions (in priority order):
- Pause auto: stops future evaluations but keeps current traffic allocation.
- Revert last step: single-click, returns traffic and opens a tiny incident note panel to record why.
- Force to baseline: immediate revert and archive rollout. Requires checkbox "I understand this will route X% of traffic away".
- Add watchlist: add a Slack/webhook alert for this rollout if it moves to rollback state.

Backlog and engineering tasks (prioritized):
1) Minimal decision engine prototype: implement threshold-led rules with required hooks and a simple state machine (Draft/Running/Paused/Aborted/Complete).
2) Visualization: timeline component with decision annotations and confidence bands + hover microcopy.
3) Simulation mode: replay last N requests to surface "what if" metric curves (fast approximate).
4) Manual override modal and operator audit log entries.
5) Messaging: in-console short descriptions + i18n-ready copy.
6) Low-volume guard: implement sample_minimum enforcement and manual override confirmation.

Open questions for the next sync:
- Do we want multiple concurrent rollouts against the same route? How do we show interacting decision effects?
- Should rollback reduce to a fixed step (e.g., -50%) or revert fully? Default should be conservative.
- How do we map rollout risk levels to auto-notifications (severity mapping).

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc is intentionally a working draft: focus feedback on the heuristics and the simplest path to prototype. Wireframes attached are rough ASCII sketches — design will refine spacing and micro-interactions.
- If engineering is comfortable with the parameter shape above we can spin a minimal prototype with simulated traffic in ~3 sprints.

Attachments / quick ASCII wireframe (very compact):
[Top] Rollout: threshold-led-demo | Running | Abort
[Left] Target: /chat/generate | Variant: v2 (5% traffic) | Mode: Threshold-led
[Mid] Safety: Primary metric: p95 (230ms) | Advance if <= +3% for 2 windows | Rollback if >= +7% for 1 window
[Right] Live: timeline sparkline [====__^^^__] decisions: 11:42 (+5%) auto-advance; 11:48 (regression) rollback -50%
